_note: Hand-written reference IR for tests/variants/brief-r5.md + api-r5.json (our own adversarial generalisation test: raw bank material with out-of-order attachments, two memos where the later partially reverses the earlier, a product-only memo, a not-yet-effective memo, footnote exceptions and a code list with numeric dispositions and retired codes). Assumption: every call date (dial_time) lies in the pilot window 2026-11-09 .. 2027-02-26 stated in the mail, so HC-26-14 (effective 2026-10-01), MF-26-04, HC-26-19 and Annex D apply and PG-26-31 (effective 2027-03-01) never applies. S1 uses deadline_unit calendar_days with the IR meaning 'latest promise date = last business day on or before today+14', which is exactly HC-26-14 point 3. MTR floor_field is the overdue-amount field itself (floor = full; a compiler that reads floor_field null as 'no part payment' would be equivalent). stage_rules are left empty (free text, ignored by ir_diff).

_expected_precedence.why: The mail defines how to read the pack: later issue date wins (attachment order is meaningless), a product-only memo wins for its product whatever the dates, a rule counts only from its effective date, footnotes travel with their rule, CP-7 dispositions are translated through Annex D and retired codes are replaced.

_expected_precedence.superseded: CP-7 2.3 'today or one of the next two business days' (within_business_days:2)
_expected_precedence.why: HC-26-14 (issued 15 Sep, effective 1 Oct) shortened the horizon; HC-26-19 (20 Oct) explicitly keeps the shorter horizon.
Later memo withdraws the extended hours and sends times back to CP-7. Partial reversal: days from HC-26-14, hours from CP-7.
Mail rule 4: a restored rule brings its footnotes back. Not expressible in callback fields: unmapped.

opening.first_sentence: Hello, this is the automated assistant of Tidewell Mutual Bank. This call is recorded.

questions.ask: Could you tell me your date of birth, please?
Thank you. And the postcode of your home address?
And finally, the last three digits of your membership number?

identity.swapped_instruction: Ask the customer to say the month as a word. That retry is not a wrong answer.
identity.failed_message: I'm sorry, I can't go any further on this call. Please ring the number on your statement or visit a branch.
identity.refusal_explanation: These questions are there to protect your account.

product_types.spoken: overdraft on your current account ending <acct_ending>

debt_intro: I'm calling from Tidewell's arrears team about overdue payments.
product_sentence: Your <spoken> is <days_late> days overdue, with <past_due> outstanding.
first_ask_single: Are you able to pay the overdue amount today?
first_ask_multi: Are you able to pay all of these today?

recording.after_promise_sentence: You'll receive a text message and an email confirming this arrangement.
recording.read_back_question: Shall I set that up for you?

fixed_sentences.deceased: I'm very sorry to hear that.
fixed_sentences.robot: I'm Tidewell Mutual Bank's automated assistant.
fixed_sentences.scam: You can check this call by ringing the number on the back of your card or on your statement.
fixed_sentences.paid: Payments can take up to two business days to show on your account.

unmapped_rules: Credit cards (CRD): where the overdue amount is 30.00 pounds or less there is no part payment; the floor is the full overdue amount (CP-7 3.3 footnote 2).
Car finance (MTR): there is no lower amount to offer; if the customer says the full amount is too much, treat it as a flat refusal (it uses an attempt) (MF-26-04).
Callbacks on 24 December and 31 December must be at 14:00 or earlier; the contact centre closes at 14:00 on those days (CP-7 2.3 footnote 1, restored by HC-26-19).
Never ask the mother's maiden name question (mmn), although verify_identity accepts it (CP-7 2.4).
Never send a retired code, although the dialler accepts them: not WEL, SYS or CBK in close_call, not SER in add_note, not desk welfare_team (Annex D; HC-26-14 point 4).
Never send the three-digit disposition number; close_call takes the mnemonic as result_code and the sub-code as reason_code, with reason_code left out for PTP and PIF (Annex D).
Say every amount in pounds and pence exactly as the system gives it; never round (CP-7 3.1).
